findings.explanation: main.tf contains only the comment `# required by Hashicorp` — there is no terraform block anywhere in the root module, so no provider source or version constraint is declared. Only example/examplea/terraform.tf (a consumer, not the module itself) pins `hashicorp/google` at exact version 7.30.0. Because the module itself has zero `terraform`/`provider_requirement` resource instances, holden's deterministic checks that would normally catch this (HLD_TF_054 required_providers must be declared, HLD_TF_002 provider version must be pinned, HLD_TF_044 google provider must be >= 4.0, HLD_TF_042 required_version must be >= 1.5) cannot evaluate at all — they need an existing block to attach a Pass/Fail to, and there isn't one, so the scan is silently Unknown rather than Fail on this exact gap. This also matters concretely now: the osadminlogin_condition/oslogin_condition variables added this session use `optional()` object attributes, which require Terraform >= 1.3 — a consumer on an older Terraform gets a confusing native error instead of a clear module-level version-floor message.
findings.title: Root module declares no `terraform`/`required_providers` block at all

findings.explanation: Every other multi-word resource label in this repo uses snake_case (compute_os_admin_login, compute_os_login, service_account_users) — visible in git status as an active rename-to-snake_case cleanup already in progress this session (google_project_iam_binding.Compute-OS-Admin-Login.tf -> compute_os_admin_login.tf, serviceAccountUsers.tf -> service_account_users.tf). `storageadmin` (storage_admin) is the one remaining compound label that wasn't touched. This is style-only, but stands out precisely because of the in-progress convention migration.
findings.remediation: Rename the resource label from `storageadmin` to `storage_admin` (and the file to google_project_iam_binding.storage_admin.tf) for consistency. Since this is a published, reusable module, renaming changes the resource's state address for any existing consumer — pair the rename with a `moved` block (`moved { from = google_project_iam_binding.storageadmin; to = google_project_iam_binding.storage_admin }`) so `terraform plan` shows no destroy/recreate for downstream callers on Terraform >= 1.1.
findings.title: `storageadmin` is the only compound-word IAM binding resource label without a separating underscore
